news.headline: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
news.story_lead: - Published 6 November 2026, 15:04 GMT Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have been climbing following an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development.
news.full_article_text: - Published 6 November 2026, 15:04 GMT Shares in artificial intelligence and technology firms have been climbing following an enormous sell-off that wiped trillions of dollars off stock values. The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock index opened higher following a market rout that began in the US on Thursday before spilling over to Asian and European markets into Friday. Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat victory in the midterm elections would mean slower artificial intelligence development. However the latest US employment figures added to a mixed picture for American markets on Friday morning, with an unexpectedly strong 165,000 jobs added to the economy in September. On Thursday, businesses closely linked to artificial intelligence development took a hammering on stock markets, particularly chip and semiconductor makers. But the Nasdaq Composite bounced back slightly on Friday, up 1.4%, reversing some of its 5.5% fall. The S&P 500, which tracks the share prices of the largest publicly-traded US companies, was up about 0.7%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was flat through the day. Nvidia shed hundreds of billions in market value on Thursday after shares slid more than 9%, but recovered some of those losses on Friday, trading up more than 3%. SpaceX and Tesla shares, which were also hammered on Thursday, saw mixed gains, up more than 8% and nearly 5% respectively. Chipmakers AMD and Micron both dropped by more than 17% on Thursday, but AMD shares had risen by about 10% on Friday while Micron was up more than 5%. However, stock markets in Asia and Europe fared worse on Friday. The Kospi in South Korea closed down 6% on Friday, with shares in chipmaker SK Hynix plunging more than 10%. European markets also fell, with the main indexes in Germany, France and Spain ending the day down. In the UK, the FTSE 100, which tracks the largest companies on the London Stock Exchange, declined 1.01%. In addition to the recent market volatility, UK traders were also digesting the latest Bank of England decision to raise interest rates and the signal that another rate rise could be on the cards to curb rising prices. Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said it had been a brutal week for markets, and the key question was whether the jump in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq would be sustained. "While no-one knows what happens next, it's clear that we've just seen a significant shift in market sentiment," he said. "Once investors have had the weekend to catch their breath, next week could give a clearer indication of whether the tech trade is going down the pan or fighting back." - Could the US midterms put a pin in the AI bubble? Published 1 hour ago - Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck Published 9 hours ago The market fluctuations come after the sweeping Democrat victory in the midterm elections. A number of Democrats campaigned for new rules and regulations for artificial intelligence (AI) and data centres, and the party has since won control of both houses of congress as well as key contests in states that have been part of the AI data centre race. US President Donald Trump on Friday reiterated his supported for what he calls "super intelligence", saying only "foolish leadership" would "say no to the riches they bring". However, there have also been concerns over whether the enormous amounts of money being spent on AI will pay off. Russ Shaw, founder of global tech advocacy firm Tech London Advocates, said the election result was sending a message that a rethink was needed on AI. "The incoming Congress is going to really focus on AI in a very dramatic way," he told the BBC's Business Today. "I'm a big fan of AI, but I'm watching what these companies are doing, and they're not communicating effectively at all, particularly in the US, about what the benefits of AI are all about." He said people were watching firms come into their communities and build data centres while their own energy costs were going up, and those companies "have to be better neighbours". Strong jobs figures could ease market fears As well as the fallout of the midterms and the plunge in artificial intelligence stocks, US traders will also be digesting the latest jobs figures. And those numbers were better than expected: US employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, well above the average monthly increase and more than double what analysts had expected. Overall the unemployment rate, which counts the number of people who are out of work but actively looking for a job, eased slightly to 4.1% from 4.2% in September . The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the unemployment rate has remained in the narrow range of 4.1% to 4.3% since March. Neil Birrell, chief investment officer at investment firm Premier Miton, said while the jobs figures may feel like second billing to the market movements they were still important. "The US economy is running hard which may mean the risks the markets are worrying about at the moment are not such a risk to the real economy as is being feared," he said. news.story_lead: Rajasthan: Kuno forest team tracking cheetah KGP-3 attacked by villagers after it kills buffalo calf A Kuno National Park forester alleged that villagers assaulted and tried to strangle him while his team tracked cheetah KGP-3 in Rajasthan’s Karauli district. A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area.
news.full_article_text: Rajasthan: Kuno forest team tracking cheetah KGP-3 attacked by villagers after it kills buffalo calf A Kuno National Park forester alleged that villagers assaulted and tried to strangle him while his team tracked cheetah KGP-3 in Rajasthan’s Karauli district. A forest team from Madhya Pradesh’s Kuno National Park, deployed to track the movements of cheetah KGP-3 after it strayed into Rajasthan’s Karauli district, was allegedly assaulted by a group of villagers following the animal’s killing of a buffalo calf, police said on Friday. A forester sustained injuries and sought police protection for the team, which is monitoring the cheetah in the Mandrayal area. Alok Prajapati (34), a forester with Kuno National Park, lodged a complaint on Tuesday against five to six unidentified villagers for allegedly assaulting members of the forest team. In his complaint, Prajapati said that the cheetah’s movement had been traced to the area under Chandelipura gram panchayat of Mandrayal police station limits, where the animal had killed a buffalo calf. Around five to six villagers allegedly approached the team and began abusing its members. They assaulted Prajapati and threatened to kill him, according to the complaint. Prajapati also sought police security for the forest team deployed for night patrolling. Prajapati told HT that an elderly man approached the team while it was patrolling the area to track the cheetah’s movements and started abusing them. “We tried to convince him and assured him that compensation would be provided for the death of the buffalo calf. Later, another man arrived and called other villagers. The attackers tried to strangle me and started pelting stones,” he alleged. Mandrayal police station station house officer Jay Prakash Singh said a case had been registered against five to six unidentified people under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). An investigation is underway to identify the accused and initiate legal action, he said.

news.full_article_text: Supreme Court appoints ex-CJI Gavai to head panel scrutinising forest rights claims in Tamil Nadu The Supreme Court has tasked a panel led by ex-CJI Bhushan Gavai with scrutinising forest rights claims under the FRA in Tamil Nadu. The Supreme Court on Friday appointed former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Bhushan R Gavai to head a special committee that will scrutinise orders passed by authorities in Tamil Nadu under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 (FRA), even as it came down hard on the state government for its prolonged failure to initiate the statutory process to identify and adjudicate the claims of forest dwellers in the ecologically sensitive Agasthyamalai landscape. A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta constituted the committee, comprising Justice Gavai as chairperson, an officer of the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and Tamil Nadu’s principal chief conservator of forests, to oversee the determination of claims by Forest-Dwelling Scheduled Tribe (FDST) and other traditional forest dwellers (OTFD). The committee will scrutinise the orders passed by competent authorities under the FRA and submit its findings to the court in a sealed cover. The court directed the state to complete the constitution of the remaining Gram Sabhas within 30 days and conclude the entire process of inviting and adjudicating claims through the statutory three-tier mechanism within five months of their constitution. The committee, in turn, has been asked to complete its scrutiny within two months of the expiry of this outer deadline. Criticising the state for its inaction, the bench observed that the process under the FRA had remained uninitiated for years even after an interim stay imposed by the Madras high court was vacated by the Supreme Court in 2016. “Apparently thus, the process under Section 6 was never initiated for years even after the lifting of the stay and seems to have been triggered only after this Court took suo motu cognizance of the prevailing situation,” it said. The bench added that the state appeared to have “woken up” only after the court directed the removal of encroachments from the Srivilliputhur-Megamalai Tiger Reserve and other reserved forests in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere. “It is clear that the State Government is primarily responsible for the delay in the process of receiving, identifying and adjudicating the claims under the FRA, 2006. Before this Court took cognizance of the encroachments in the forest area, even the Gram Sabhas had not been constituted,” said the bench, granting the state what it described as a “last opportunity” to complete the exercise. The committee has been empowered to issue necessary directions to authorities for expeditious disposal of claims. The state will also have to submit monthly progress reports to it. Senior counsel Jaideep Gupta appeared for the state government, while senior advocate Sriram Panchu represented the state’s department of Social Justice. The directions came in proceedings concerning large-scale encroachments in the Agasthyamalai landscape, where the court had, in its May 29 judgment, ordered a structured and time-bound process for eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration. The latest proceedings arose from competing claims over the application of the FRA to people residing in or cultivating land in the Megamalai region. While the state argued that claims under the FRA needed to be examined before eviction, the court accepted the amicus curiae and senior advocate K Parmeshwar’s submission that the statutory protection could not be extended indiscriminately to everyone occupying or cultivating forest land. The bench clarified that two categories of occupants identified by the state itself would be excluded from consideration under the Act. These are people cultivating forest land while maintaining only temporary residence within it and those residing outside the forest boundary but cultivating land inside it. The state’s affidavit had identified 4,594 occupants spread across 5,072.64 hectares, of whom 2,643 were engaged in silk cotton cultivation over 3,637.83 hectares. Of these, 1,595 persons were permanently residing in the forest and cultivating land, 232 had temporary residence while cultivating, and 2,767 were residing outside the forest boundary but cultivating within it. The court said the latter two categories could not qualify as FDST or OTFD merely on the basis of cultivation, since the statutory definitions required claimants to primarily reside in and depend on forest land. For OTFDs, the law specifically requires residence and dependence for at least three generations, or 75 years, prior to December 13, 2005. The court also rejected the state’s attempt to justify silk cotton cultivation as a traditional minor forest produce protected under the FRA. It noted that the government had relied on historical cultivation and agricultural records but had failed to produce any specific notification recognising silk cotton as minor forest produce under the Act or any other forest law. Distinguishing between naturally occurring forest produce and commercial cultivation, the bench said the material suggested that silk cotton had been introduced as a planned plantation rather than traditionally collected as minor forest produce. “The concept of planned cultivation of commercial crop is totally contrary to the very concept of a naturally occurring minor forest produce,” said the bench, adding that commercial crop cultivation could not become a recognised forest right to justify continued occupation of reserved forest land. It further asked the CEC to examine the state’s claim that silk cotton qualified as minor forest produce and investigate the circumstances surrounding cultivation by people residing outside the forest boundary, including whether others were financing or facilitating such activity. The Supreme Court on Friday appointed former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Bhushan R Gavai to head a special committee that will scrutinise orders passed by authorities in Tamil Nadu under the Forest Rights Act, 2006 (FRA), even as it came down hard on the state government for its prolonged failure to initiate the statutory process to identify and adjudicate the claims of forest dwellers in the ecologically sensitive Agasthyamalai landscape.

A bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta constituted the committee, comprising Justice Gavai as chairperson, an officer of the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and Tamil Nadu’s principal chief conservator of forests, to oversee the determination of claims by Forest-Dwelling Scheduled Tribe (FDST) and other traditional forest dwellers (OTFD). The committee will scrutinise the orders passed by competent authorities under the FRA and submit its findings to the court in a sealed cover.

The court directed the state to complete the constitution of the remaining Gram Sabhas within 30 days and conclude the entire process of inviting and adjudicating claims through the statutory three-tier mechanism within five months of their constitution. The committee, in turn, has been asked to complete its scrutiny within two months of the expiry of this outer deadline.

Criticising the state for its inaction, the bench observed that the process under the FRA had remained uninitiated for years even after an interim stay imposed by the Madras high court was vacated by the Supreme Court in 2016.

“Apparently thus, the process under Section 6 was never initiated for years even after the lifting of the stay and seems to have been triggered only after this Court took suo motu cognizance of the prevailing situation,” it said.

The bench added that the state appeared to have “woken up” only after the court directed the removal of encroachments from the Srivilliputhur-Megamalai Tiger Reserve and other reserved forests in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere.

news.full_article_text:
### Satellite Analysis of Iranian Military Infrastructure

Recent satellite imagery analyzed by British intelligence firm MAIAR, with additional evaluations from Janes and the Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI), reveals ongoing construction and repair activities across strategic Iranian military facilities. Despite extensive US and Israeli air strikes targeting defense complexes, Iranian forces are restoring damaged structures and expanding underground networks to safeguard critical military assets.

### Primary Sites Under Repair and Construction

- **Garmdareh Military Base (Karaj):** Located near Tehran, satellite imagery shows excavation, vehicle movement, and newly constructed portals for an underground facility.
- **Shahroud Base:** Situated in northern Iran, digging and new building construction indicate efforts by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) to relocate missile manufacturing facilities underground.
- **Parchin Military Complex:** East of Tehran, debris from previous air strikes has been cleared. At the Taleghan 2 facility within Parchin, an underground bunker has been repaired and reinforced with concrete.
- **Kermanshah Missile Base:** Located in western Iran near the border with Iraq, destroyed facilities have been covered with new roofs.
- **Fordo Region (Qom):** Excavations and construction work have been observed outside tunnel entrances close to the Fordo underground uranium enrichment facility.

### Strategic Implications and Expert Findings

Defense analysts, including former CIA analyst Jim Lamson and CSIS expert Mark Cancian, note that Iran is prioritizing military capability reconstruction and underground fortification over economic rehabilitation. Transitioning military manufacturing and storage into subterranean facilities reduces visibility for foreign satellite intelligence and mitigates vulnerability to precision aerial attacks.

### ईरानी सैन्य बुनियादी ढांचे पर उपग्रह विश्लेषण

ब्रिटिश इंटेलिजेंस कंपनी MAIAR द्वारा विश्लेषित और जेन्स (Janes) तथा फॉरेन पॉलिसी रिसर्च इंस्टीट्यूट (FPRI) के इनपुट वाले हालिया उपग्रह चित्र प्रमुख ईरानी सैन्य सुविधाओं में महत्वपूर्ण निर्माण और मरम्मत गतिविधियों को उजागर करते हैं। अमेरिकी और इजराइली हवाई हमलों से कई रक्षा परिसरों को नुकसान पहुंचने के बावजूद, ईरानी बल सक्रिय रूप से अपने ठिकानों को बहाल कर रहे हैं और परिचालन क्षमताओं की सुरक्षा के लिए भूमिगत बुनियादी ढांचे का निर्माण कर रहे हैं।

### मरम्मत और निर्माण के तहत प्राथमिक स्थल

- **गर्मदारेह सैन्य अड्डा (करज):** तेहरान के पास स्थित, उपग्रह तस्वीरें उत्खनन, वाहनों की आवाजाही और नए सुरंग द्वारों को दर्शाती हैं जो एक भूमिगत सुविधा के निर्माण का संकेत देते हैं।
- **शाहरूद अड्डा:** उत्तरी ईरान में स्थित, खुदाई और नई संरचनाएं दर्शाती हैं कि इस्लामिक रिवोल्यूशनरी गार्ड कॉर्प्स (IRGC) मिसाइल उत्पादन सुविधाओं को भूमिगत स्थानांतरित करने का प्रयास कर रही है।
- **परचिन सैन्य परिसर:** तेहरान के पूर्व में स्थित, क्षतिग्रस्त संरचनाओं को साफ कर दिया गया है, और तालेघान 2 स्थल पर महत्वपूर्ण कार्यों में एक भूमिगत बंकर की कंक्रीट सुदृढ़ीकरण मरम्मत शामिल है।
- **केरमनशाह मिसाइल अड्डा:** इराक सीमा के पास पश्चिमी ईरान में स्थित, नष्ट हुई सुविधाओं पर नए रूफ (छत) लगाए गए हैं।
- **फोर्दो क्षेत्र (कोम):** फोर्दो भूमिगत यूरेनियम संवर्धन स्थल के पास सुरंग द्वारों के बाहर नए उत्खनन और निर्माण कार्य दर्ज किए गए हैं।

### रणनीतिक निहितार्थ और विशेषज्ञ निष्कर्ष

पूर्व सीआईए विश्लेषक जिम लेमसन और सीएसआईएस सैन्य विशेषज्ञ मार्क कैनसियन सहित रक्षा विश्लेषकों का कहना है कि ईरान आर्थिक पुनर्वास की तुलना में सैन्य क्षमता के पुनर्निर्माण और भूमिगत सुदृढ़ीकरण को प्राथमिकता दे रहा है। बुनियादी ढांचे को भूमिगत स्थानांतरित करने से विदेशी उपग्रह निगरानी जटिल हो जाती है और भविष्य के हवाई हमलों से परिसंपत्तियों की सुरक्षा होती है।
